name: Glyph Lines
definition: Samples a vector field on a 2D grid at a fixed x-coordinate `x`, and renders each vector as a line segment (two vertices) centered at the sample point, scaled by magnitude and colored by magnitude.
summary: Glyph Lines is a sparse 3D vector field visualization technique that renders samples on a 2D grid as line segments, encoding direction and magnitude into geometric primitives for efficient slice analysis.
